title: Project 2025 Calls for Ending Head Start and School Meals, Eliminating Title I Funds
description_short: Project 2025 Calls for Ending Head Start and School Meals, Eliminating Title I Funds
description_medium: The National Education Association describes Project 2025 as a Heritage Foundation blueprint for a second Trump presidency. It reports that the plan calls for ending Head Start and universal free school meals, and eliminating Title I funding for high-poverty schools in favor of state block grants. The article documents proposed policies; it does not show that the administration implemented these changes.
description_long: Project 2025 is a Heritage Foundation blueprint for a second Trump presidency, according to the National Education Association (NEA). The NEA reports that the plan calls for ending Head Start and universal free school meals and eliminating Title I funding for high-poverty schools, with block grants to states in its place. It describes Title I as federal financial help for high-poverty schools and districts, provided since 1965. The article says Head Start served 833,000 children in fiscal year 2022; that figure describes the program before the proposal, not children affected by an implemented change. The record therefore describes a policy proposal, not a completed action by the Trump administration. The cited reporting establishes what Project 2025 proposes and frames potential effects, but does not show that the administration ended Head Start, universal free school meals, or Title I funding, or establish the programs’ current status.

supported_facts.quote: “Project 2025 also calls for the end of the Head Start program, which served 833,000 children in fiscal year 2022, and would end universal free school meals that provide food security to millions of children.”
supported_facts.supports: The blueprint proposes ending Head Start and universal free school meals; 833,000 is the historical Head Start service figure for FY2022.

supported_facts.quote: “Since 1965, Title I has provided critical financial help to high-poverty schools and districts. Project 2025 plans to eliminate Title I funding entirely. In its place, states will receive no-strings-attached block grants with zero regulations or oversight.”
supported_facts.supports: Title I provides support to high-poverty schools and the blueprint proposes replacing its funding with state block grants.

supported_facts.quote: “The 900+ page blueprint for another Trump presidency, produced by the Heritage Foundation”
supported_facts.supports: The source characterizes Project 2025 as a Heritage Foundation blueprint for a future Trump presidency.

limitations: This October 4, 2024 article describes proposals and projected effects; it does not establish subsequent implementation or present-day program status.
